name: WHOOP
h1_tail: Funding Rounds, Share Prices and Ownership
description: WHOOP is privately held and has no ticker. Review the price of each funding round, its investors, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: WHOOP is a privately held wearable technology company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the prices at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $575 million Series G round announced on March 31, 2026, valued the company at $10.1 billion.

Founded in 2012 and based in Boston, WHOOP sells a membership that includes a wearable sensor and an app reporting on sleep, recovery, strain and other health measures. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round.
round_notes: Collaborative Fund led the Series G. In March 2026, WHOOP said it had ended 2025 with an annual bookings run rate of $1.1 billion, up 103% from a year earlier; that figure is the company's own.

A round price reflects what investors paid for the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Collaborative Fund led the Series G, with participation from Qatar Investment Authority, Mubadala, Abbott, Mayo Clinic and Macquarie Capital, as well as athletes including Cristiano Ronaldo and LeBron James. SoftBank Vision Fund 2 led the Series F and IVP the Series E. Other investors include Foundry Group, Accomplice, Promus Ventures and GP Bullhound.
spv_sentence: SEC filings show one special purpose vehicle formed to invest in WHOOP, organized in 2020.
sources: Sources: WHOOP's Series F announcement (August 30, 2021); reports by TechCrunch (March 2026) and Front Office Sports (October 2020); and SEC Form D filings.
